title: Arakhin 2 - Children's Obligation in Misvot

chapters.title: Who can make or be the object of a valuation
chapters.about: Mishna, Kohanim, Nevi'im, Yisraelim, Tumtum, Androgynos

chapters.title: Analyzing the term Hakol in the Mishna
Semicha and Temura for an heir
Korban Re'iya and the half-slave status
chapters.about: Beit HaMikdash, half-slave, Bet Hillel, Bet Shammai

summary: Rabbi Hidary explores the opening Mishna of Masekhet Arakhin, which discusses the laws of valuations and the general inclusion of various individuals in specific mitzvot. He analyzes the use of the term 'Hakol' in this Mishna and other Mishnaic and Beraita sources to determine which specific groups or individuals are included in mitzvot such as Semicha, Temura, Sukkah, Lulav, Tzitzit, Tefillin, and Korban Re'iya.
questions: Who is included in the obligation to perform valuations?
Can a minor or someone with limited mental capacity be the object of a valuation?
Does an heir have the same obligations as the original owner regarding Semicha and Temura?
At what point does a child become obligated in mitzvot like Sukkah or Lulav?
How does the status of a person who is half-slave and half-free affect their obligation to bring a Korban Re'iya?
